media.alt: An adult African catfish lying on a concrete surface, showing its long body, long dorsal fin and barbels
media.caption: An adult African catfish (Clarias gariepinus). Notice the long, eel-like body and the fin running along most of its back.

media.alt: Close-up from above of an African catfish head with long barbels around the mouth
media.caption: The flattened head and barbels (whisker-like feelers) of an African catfish, photographed in Indonesia, where the species is also farmed.

media.alt: Historical colour drawing of an African catfish seen from the side and slightly above
media.caption: A 19th-century scientific drawing of the African catfish. Drawings like this make body parts easy to see.
media.credit: Illustrations of the Zoology of South Africa (author unknown)

media.alt: Several young dark African catfish wriggling on wet ground
media.caption: Young African catfish. These were wild fish, not farmed fingerlings, but they show the shape of young catfish.

media.alt: A lined fish pond with netting over it and fish rippling the surface, beside a grassy bank in Ilorin
media.caption: A fish pond near the Asa dam in Egbejila, Ilorin, Nigeria, covered with netting.

media.alt: Looking down into a tiled concrete tank full of catfish swimming in green water with floating feed
media.caption: A concrete fish tank with catfish feeding.

media.alt: Close-up of a tarpaulin fish tank filled with greenish water reflecting the sky
media.caption: Inside a tarpaulin fish tank.

media.alt: Two tarpaulin fish tanks on metal frames in a walled backyard with banana plants
media.caption: Two tarpaulin (collapsible) fish tanks set up in a backyard.

media.alt: A hand-operated borehole pump on a concrete platform surrounded by grass
media.caption: A hand-operated borehole pump in Irawo, Atisbo LGA, Oyo State, Nigeria.

media.alt: A covered, padlocked hand-dug well with a concrete ring in a shaded compound
media.caption: A covered hand-dug well in Ilorin, Nigeria.
